messages.author: b78b2bf83f051218
messages.subject: Facet with Multiple Span Parameters
parts:
Hi all,

I'm trying to make a faceted plot, plotting the same points in each facet, but applying a different span to stat_smooth.  I'm looking for something like this:

require(ggplot2)
x <- runif(100,min=-4*pi, max=4*pi)
df <- data.frame(x=x,y=sin(x))

qplot(df$x, df$y)+stat_smooth(span=.4)
qplot(df$x, df$y)+stat_smooth(span=.5)
qplot(df$x, df$y)+stat_smooth(span=.6)
qplot(df$x, df$y)+stat_smooth(span=.7)

but with each plot in its own facet.

Any ideas?

messages.author: f4249b01b99d0091
messages.subject: Re: Facet with Multiple Span Parameters
parts:
I think you'll need to start by doing the four stat_smooth calls in
sequence and saving the results of each. For an example of this see
http://stackoverflow.com/questions/9789871/method-to-extract-stat-smooth-line-fit

Then you can build your faceted plot using geom_point (same data in
all panels), geom_line (varies by panel, uses stat_smooth outputs),
and geom_ribbon (same).

Ben

messages.author: 0c39e60ddb38622b
messages.subject: Re: Facet with Multiple Span Parameters
parts:
Hi:

As Ben mentioned, you want to save the individual ggplots to separate
objects. You can use the grid.arrange() function in the gridExtra
package to plot them in sequence.

Starting with your code,

p1 <- qplot(df$x, df$y)+stat_smooth(span=.4) + ggtitle(span = 0.4)
p2 <- qplot(df$x, df$y)+stat_smooth(span=.5) + ggtitle(span = 0.5)
p3 <- qplot(df$x, df$y)+stat_smooth(span=.6) + ggtitle(span = 0.6)
p4 <- qplot(df$x, df$y)+stat_smooth(span=.7) + ggtitle(span = 0.7)

library(gridExtra)
grid.arrange(p1, p2, p3, p4, ncol = 2)

A more efficient way to do this (using the DRY principle) is to write
a function to do each plot with a variable span, save the plots as a
list and then use grid.arrange(). Here's one way; I changed the data
frame name to avoid potential conflicts with the df() function.

DF <- data.frame(x=x, y=sin(x))

# Function to draw a single loess smooth; span is its formal argument
plotfun <- function(span = 0.5)
{
require(ggplot2)
ggplot(DF, aes(x = x, y = y)) +
geom_point() +
stat_smooth(span = span) +
ggtitle(paste0("span = ", span))
}

# Produce a vector of spans
spans <- seq(0.4, 0.7, by = 0.1)

# Use the lapply function to recursively call plotfun() with different spans
plots <- lapply(spans, function(x) plotfun(x))

require(gridExtra)
# use the do.call() function to invoke grid.arrange() since the plots
are in a list
suppressMessages(do.call(grid.arrange, plots))


BTW: DRY = "Don't Repeat Yourself", in case you didn't already know that.
Dennis
